label: FACIS DSP — IAM Hub
info:
NF-1 follow-on: MongoDB-backed Identity Hub. Drains this connector's
in-memory issuance handoff queue (global.get('identityHubPending'),
pushed to by tab-dsp-iam-issuance's dsp-iam-issuance-vc-push) into a
`credentials` Mongo collection, and serves it back out via a small read
API, including the DCP Credential-Service pull endpoint counterparties
use to fetch this connector's own Participant VC.

GET  /iam/hub/credentials       — list, filtered by ?type/?issuer/?subject/?status
GET  /iam/hub/credentials/:id   — single credential by _id
GET  /iam/hub/participant       — this connector's own ParticipantCredential
                                   (DCP Credential-Service pull endpoint)

Uses node-red-contrib-mongodb4@3.4.0 (Task 8's provisioning). That
package registers exactly two node types: the `mongodb4-client` config
node (connection) and a single `mongodb4` operation node (mode +
collection + operation are all set per-node; msg.payload must be an
ARRAY of the driver call's arguments, e.g. `[filter]` for find or
`[docsArray]` for insertMany) — there is no separate mongodb4-in/-out/
-find node family, despite that being a common Node-RED contrib
convention elsewhere. Verified directly against the published package
tarball (src/mongodb4.js + mongodb4.html + examples/example-1.json),
not guessed.

The `mongodb4-client` config node has no built-in msg/env-typed field for
its URI — its `uri` property (Advanced Connection URI tab) is a plain
string, populated here with Node-RED's standard `${ENV_VAR}` deploy-time
environment-variable substitution syntax (a core Node-RED feature, not
specific to function nodes) pointing at env var DSP_MONGO_URI (Task 8).
`dbName` is set separately (the driver always calls `client.db(dbName)`
regardless of any db path segment already present in the URI) to
`identity_hub`, matching the default DSP_MONGO_URI rendered by
templates/orce-secret.yaml (`mongodb://<release>-mongo:27017/identity_hub`).

Admin-write gating (Keycloak-JWKS bearer check on the drain/write path)
is a documented, accepted gap: the drain node only consumes THIS
connector's own internal issuance queue (global context, not externally
reachable), so it is not itself an injectable surface. No JWKS-verification
pattern exists elsewhere in this codebase to honestly reuse (see
dsp-iam-issuance-vc-guard's own comment on the same gap for the write
side of tab-dsp-iam-issuance). Flagged here as a fast-follow, not invented.

See orce/tests/flows/iam-hub-query-filter.spec.js for the mirrored pure
logic dsp-iam-hub-query-fn's buildCredentialFilter must stay
byte-identical to (NoSQL injection whitelist guard).

name: drain identityHubPending
build filter (whitelist)
build {_id} filter
build participant filter
unwrap single-item result
build find args
build + sign status list VC
Bearer shared-secret guard
build updateOne args
build response from UpdateResult
build 502
